claim: A single vesicle-vesicle system with reconstituted SNARE and synaptotagmin-1 proteoliposomes was used to decipher the temporal sequence of membrane states upon Ca2+-injection at 250-500 μM on a 100-ms timescale.
source_text: Here, we used a single vesicle–vesicle system with reconstituted SNARE and synaptotagmin-1 proteoliposomes to decipher the temporal sequence of membrane states upon Ca 2+ -injection at 250–500 μM on a 100-ms timescale.
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes the experimental system and methods used in the study, which is supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: All instances of Ca2+-triggered immediate fusion started from a membrane-membrane point-contact and proceeded to complete fusion without discernible hemifusion intermediates.
source_text: Remarkably, all instances of Ca 2+ -triggered immediate fusion started from a membrane–membrane point-contact and proceeded to complete fusion without discernible hemifusion intermediates.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding supported by the single vesicle-vesicle microscopy experiments and cryo-EM imaging data presented in Figures 2, 3, and 4.

claim: Pathways that involved a stable hemifusion diaphragm only resulted in fusion after many seconds, if at all.
source_text: In contrast, pathways that involved a stable hemifusion diaphragm only resulted in fusion after many seconds, if at all.
evidence_reasoning: This finding is supported by the fluorescence intensity time traces shown in Figure 4B and the temporal analysis of fusion events.

claim: When complexin was included, the Ca2+-triggered fusion network shifted towards the immediate pathway, effectively synchronizing fusion, especially at lower Ca2+-concentration.
source_text: When complexin was included, the Ca 2+ -triggered fusion network shifted towards the immediate pathway, effectively synchronizing fusion, especially at lower Ca 2+ -concentration.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by the experimental data comparing fusion with and without complexin shown in Figure 6.

claim: Synaptic proteins may have evolved to select the immediate pathway out of a heterogeneous network of possible membrane fusion pathways.
source_text: Synaptic proteins may have evolved to select this immediate pathway out of a heterogeneous network of possible membrane fusion pathways.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative evolutionary interpretation based on the observed data about fusion pathways.

claim: Synaptic vesicle fusion is unique in that it is both regulated and fast, in the order of a millisecond.
source_text: Among these biological processes, synaptic vesicle fusion is unique in that it is both regulated and fast, in the order of a millisecond (Meinrenken et al., 2003).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Meinrenken et al., 2003 and represents established scientific knowledge about synaptic vesicle fusion.

claim: Upon an action potential, at most one synaptic vesicle undergoes exocytosis in a synapse among the readily releasable pool.
source_text: Upon an action potential, at most one synaptic vesicle undergoes exocytosis in a synapse among the readily releasable pool (Dobrunz and Stevens, 1997)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Dobrunz and Stevens, 1997.

claim: A hemifusion intermediate is defined as a membrane state where the outer leaflets of the two juxtaposed membranes exchange lipids.
source_text: A hemifusion intermediate is defined as a membrane state where the outer leaflets of the two juxtaposed membranes exchange lipids; examples include an hourglass shaped 'stalk' and an elongated hemifusion diaphragm.
evidence_reasoning: This is a standard definition in the field of membrane fusion based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Model calculations suggested that a hemifusion diaphragm is an energetically relatively stable, long-lived intermediate.
source_text: Model calculations suggested that a hemifusion diaphragm is an energetically relatively stable, long-lived intermediate, and that the direct pathway from stalk to fusion pore may be faster (Kuzmin et al., 2001).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Kuzmin et al., 2001 describing model calculations.

claim: Several key proteins cooperate in Ca2+-triggered synaptic vesicle fusion, including SNAREs, synaptotagmin 1, complexin, and SM proteins.
source_text: Several key proteins cooperate in Ca2+-triggered synaptic vesicle fusion, including the soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment protein receptors (SNAREs) (Söllner et al., 1993; Sutton et al., 1998; Jahn and Scheller, 2006), the Ca2+ sensor synaptotagmin 1, the activator/inhibitor complexin, and SM proteins (Rizo and Rosenmund, 2008; Südhof and Rothman, 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: SNARE proteins can promote membrane fusion via hemifusion intermediates, as inferred from lipid-mixing studies with proteoliposomes.
source_text: SNARE proteins can promote membrane fusion via hemifusion intermediates, as inferred from lipid-mixing studies with proteoliposomes where fluorescent labels measure the exchange of components between lipid bilayers (Weber et al., 1998; Reese and Mayer, 2005; Xu et al., 2005; Schaub et al., 2006; Liu et al., 2008).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous lipid-mixing studies.

claim: Content mixing is not necessarily correlated with lipid mixing for biological membrane fusion.
source_text: Several previous studies implied that content mixing is not necessarily correlated with lipid mixing for biological membrane fusion
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on inference from multiple previous studies cited in the text.

claim: Neuronal SNAREs alone do not produce much content mixing, although they readily induce lipid mixing.
source_text: neuronal SNAREs alone do not produce much content mixing, although they readily induce lipid mixing (Bowen et al., 2004; Kyoung et al., 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Bowen et al., 2004 and Kyoung et al., 2011.

claim: The system achieved a Ca2+ sensitivity in the 250-500 μM range after improvements in optical instrumentation and protein expression and purification.
source_text: After improvements in optical instrumentation as well as protein expression and purification, here we achieved a Ca2+ sensitivity in the 250–500 μM range.
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes the technical achievement of the experimental system, supported by the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The Ca2+ range of 250-500 μM is reasonably close to the physiological concentration range (starting at 10 μM and saturating at several 100 μM).
source_text: This Ca2+ range is reasonably close to the physiological concentration range (starting at 10 μM and saturating at several 100 μM) (Heidelberger et al., 1994)
evidence_reasoning: This claim compares the experimental Ca2+ range to physiological values cited from Heidelberger et al., 1994.

claim: Three characteristic changes in membrane state were observed: immediate fusion, delayed fusion, and hemifusion-only.
source_text: We observed three characteristic changes in membrane state, including instances of immediate fusion (a correlate with synchronous neurotransmitter release), delayed fusion (a correlate with asynchronous release), and hemifusion-only (i.e., without complete fusion) during the observation period of 50 s.
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes the experimental observations shown in Figure 1B and is supported by the fluorescence intensity time traces.

claim: For the minimal system consisting of only SNAREs and synaptotagmin 1, immediate fusion instances were in the minority.
source_text: Overall, for this very minimal system consisting of only SNAREs and synaptotagmin 1, immediate fusion instances were in the minority, followed by delayed fusion instances, and then hemifusion-only instances (Figure 1C).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by the quantitative data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Ca2+ triggered fusion depended on the presence of both functional SNAREs and synaptotagmin 1.
source_text: As we had shown previously, Ca2+ triggered fusion depended on the presence of both functional SNAREs and synaptotagmin 1, for example, mutation of one of the Ca2+ binding sites of synaptotagmin 1 greatly reduced the amount of immediate fusion and disruption of SNARE complex formation prevented both docking and fusion (Kyoung et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by previous data from Kyoung et al., 2011, including mutation experiments.

claim: Some fusion occurred after Ca2+-addition, shifting the diameter distribution of vesicles towards larger vesicles.
source_text: As expected from our single-vesicle microscopy fusion experiments with identical vesicle preparations, some fusion occurred after Ca2+-addition, shifting the diameter distribution of vesicles observed in the cryo-EM images towards larger vesicles than before Ca2+ addition

claim: The mean diameter increased from 61.3 ± 18.6 nm to 65.1 ± 23.9 nm after Ca2+ addition.
